This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Waltz in one**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read the band's last four bars on the staff underneath. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

For a quick 3/4. The root on 1 and light, short chords on 2 and 3, the third beat the lighter. The bars go in fours: the first leans, the third a little, and the fourth grows into the next phrase. In 4/4 it is boom-chick.

It belongs in *Waltz (in one)*, *Boom-chick*, *Folk carol* and *Hymn (four parts)*. Here it is in the waltz (in one) style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-pad.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah

Short chords on the beats the bass leaves free: 2 and 4 in 4/4, 2 and 3 in a waltz. Goes with the Root and fifth bass line.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-oompah.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Waltz in one, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Root on 1, light short chords on 2 and 3, the third the lightest. It is felt in one: one big beat a bar. The four bars of a phrase lean, rest, lean a little, and grow into the next phrase.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Waltz in one","opts":{"compRhythm":"waltz"}},{"label":"Boom-chick / oom-pah-pah (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"oompah"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 150 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="150" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Waltz in one","opts":{"compRhythm":"waltz"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="150" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Waltz in one","opts":{"compRhythm":"waltz"}}]'></div>
